title: Chemical potentials from structure factors: I. Neutral multi-component mixtures
authors: Roya Savoj, Xiaoyu Wang, Musahid Ahmed, Bingqing Cheng
abstract: The chemical potentials of multi-component mixtures underlie many physical and chemical phenomena, but remain challenging to compute. The S0 method enables the computation of chemical potentials from equilibrium molecular dynamics simulations, by leveraging the thermodynamic relationship between particle number fluctuations and derivatives of chemical potentials, followed by numerical integration along different compositions. Here we generalize the S0 method from two-component mixtures to neutral multi-component mixtures. We first extend the statistical mechanical formalism to high-dimensional compositional space, and then introduce a Gaussian process integration scheme combined with active learning to efficiently integrate chemical potentials and sample diverse compositions. We use this method to compute the mixing free energies of a molten metal alloy, and the solubilities of two paracetamol polymorphs in water-ethanol solvents. The extended S0 method provides a practical and scalable route for computing chemical potentials in neutral bulk multi-component mixtures from atomistic simulations.
summary: This paper presents an extended S0 method that overcomes the difficulty of calculating chemical potentials in complex multi-component mixtures. It achieves this by combining statistical mechanical fluctuation theorems with advanced Gaussian Process regression techniques, allowing for robust and efficient extrapolation across high-dimensional compositional spaces.
main_problem: The primary challenge addressed is the accurate computation of chemical potentials ($\mu$) for multi-component mixtures from atomistic simulations, as standard methods struggle in high-dimensional compositional space.
main_result: The authors developed an extended S0 method combined with Gaussian Process (GP) regression and Active Learning to provide a scalable route for computing mixing free energies and chemical potentials in neutral bulk mixtures.
method: The methodology extends the S0 approach by using particle number fluctuations derived from structure factors ($S_0^{\alpha eta}$) to build derivative matrices, which are then globally reconstructed using GP regression informed by active learning sampling.
model_or_system: The method is applied theoretically and computationally to model systems ranging from molten metal alloys (e.g., Fe-Cu-Ni) to molecular mixtures like paracetamol polymorphs in water-ethanol solvents.
key_observables: Chemical potentials ($\mu$), mixing free energies ($G_{	ext{mix}}$), partial static structure factors ($S_0^{\alpha eta}$), and the uncertainty estimates derived from GP regression (covariance).

main_assumptions: The method is initially restricted to neutral components; the use of GP regression assumes that function values and their gradients can be accurately modeled from sparse data points.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the application of GP regression using both function and gradient data, showing how active learning refines predictions. Other figures compare computed mixing free energies ($G_{mix}$) against established models and track component chemical potential evolution during simulations.
paper_structure: The paper builds from the theoretical foundation (S0 method generalization) to the computational implementation (GP regression with Active Learning), demonstrating its application first to metal alloys, and subsequently to molecular solubility problems like paracetamol polymorphs in mixed solvents.
why_interesting: While focused on classical statistical mechanics, the reliance on advanced machine learning techniques (Gaussian Processes, Active Learning) for data extrapolation makes it highly relevant to modern computational physics approaches used across many-body systems.
